answerable: Timing (travel-time lag) between a surface infiltration event and its arrival as recharge flux at the water table, using a coupled ELM (surface energy/water balance + top boundary flux) to PFLOTRAN (Richards-equation vadose zone) model
Vertical soil moisture and matric potential propagation through the unsaturated zone
How recharge lag varies with vadose-zone thickness and soil texture across the Naches valley/uplands

parsed.n_justification: Four columns span the dominant hydrogeologic gradient across the Naches basin: (1) riparian floodplain with shallow water table and coarse alluvium, (2) valley terrace with moderate depth, (3) upland glacial/colluvial slope with deep water table and finer soils, and (4) a coarse-outwash bench. This captures how vadose-zone thickness and texture control the infiltration-to-recharge lag while keeping the campaign tractable.
requires_capabilities: ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling via Alquimia/PETSc interface for variably-saturated (Richards equation) vadose-zone flow
Deep 1-D PFLOTRAN column extending from land surface to prescribed water table (Dirichlet/seepage bottom boundary at ZWT)
Column-specific water-table depth (observed well or regional model) to set the lower boundary
High-frequency (sub-daily) history output to resolve infiltration pulse timing and recharge arrival
Tracer/age capability in PFLOTRAN (optional) to explicitly compute infiltration-to-recharge travel time
assumptions: Water-table depths assumed representative: floodplain ~2 m, terrace ~8 m, upland slope ~25 m, outwash bench ~15 m (replace with observed values if available)
1-D vertical vadose-zone flow adequate; lateral flow and river-aquifer exchange neglected
20-year spin-up/forcing (2000-2020) using GSWP3/CLMNCEP-style atmospheric forcing to equilibrate deep moisture profiles before analyzing event-based recharge lag
'Today's infiltration' interpreted as an identified rainfall/snowmelt event whose recharge signal is tracked to ZWT; timing reported as lag between QINFL peak and QRECHARGE peak per column
Soil hydraulic parameters (van Genuchten) assigned by texture class and depth-varying to match alluvial vs. upland stratigraphy
